purpose: Resolve the largest listed-task resource definition before inventing a seasonal workability constraint.
scope: One finite primary-source screen of Columella De re rustica bookII, the already relevant2.12 task-count passage and2.4 ploughing-method passage. At most one existing named public text witness of that book, with two focused sections; no new source family or quantitative parameter search.
questions: What unit does a prescribed ploughing day claim: human operator, crew/yoke service, or another accounting basis? Which soil, implement, animal service, pass count and quality conditions belong to the count? Which simultaneous human and draft resources would a seasonal model need, and which rates or quantities remain unsupported?
source_handling: Preserve witness identity, exact section locators and source/transcription distinctions. If an edition/translation or passage is unavailable, record that access gap. Do not repair prior task counts or infer unprinted numerical resource coefficients silently.
deliverable: A concise plough resource contract distinguishing evidenced prescription, scenario conversion and missing human/draft/workability inputs; explicit decision about which resource equations can be implemented with supplied assumptions. No automatic universal task-date or animal-budget adoption.
exclusions: No new scenario/model run, hours recalibration, workforce or draft allocation, new crop mix, modern handling-rate research, complete occupation claim, reserved evidence pool, atlas/default change or climate development.
